answer: Timber-provenance registration: each agent identity must present a physical shipment record whose timber was cut by a specific sawmill, signed at the mill and cross-checked against that mill's monthly output ledger. A sparrow cannot be split into two shipments, so one operator cannot mint extra identities from the same batch without a second mill logging duplicate output. An attacker must bribe or compromise independent mills, each with its own audited vault of records, making every fake identity cost a real colluding facility plus forged ledger entries.
